items.prompt: A stateless REST API runs on one server that is at 85% CPU and is a single point of failure.
items.why: Stateless tier plus a capacity and availability problem → add servers behind a load balancer with health checks.

items.prompt: A distributed in-memory cache with 20 nodes must route each key to the node that stores it, and nodes are added during peak hours.
items.why: The request must reach the node that owns the key, and membership changes → consistent hashing, not a key-agnostic LB.

items.prompt: Requests to an inference service vary from 50 ms to 30 s; with round robin some servers queue up while others idle.
items.why: Highly variable request cost → change the LB algorithm to least connections (or power of two choices).

items.prompt: Nightly report generation jobs take minutes each and arrive in bursts of thousands; users only need an email when one finishes.
items.why: Slow, bursty and asynchronous ('email when done') → enqueue the jobs and let workers pull at their own pace.

items.prompt: /api/* must go to the API service and /img/* to the image service, both behind one public hostname with TLS.
items.why: Routing on HTTP path plus TLS termination → an L7 load balancer / reverse proxy.

items.prompt: A partner integration may call you at most 20 times per second; extra calls must get HTTP 429.
items.why: Rejecting by policy per client is rate limiting. An LB spreads requests but never refuses them.

items.prompt: Users in Europe and Asia should hit the nearest healthy region, and traffic must shift automatically if a region fails.
items.why: Steering dynamic traffic to the nearest healthy region → global load balancing (DNS / anycast) in front of the regional LBs.
